    Id: discussion.Id,
    IndividualNote: discussion.IndividualNote,
    Resolvable: discussion.Resolvable,

confirmed.summary: gitlab_list_badges validates the project/group mutual-exclusivity using IsNullOrEmpty but then branches on `project is not null`, so an empty-string project with a valid group silently queries the wrong (empty) project instead of the supplied group.
confirmed.reasoning:
Read src/GitlabMCP.Tools/ProjectsTools.cs lines 255-300 directly. The quoted code matches the file exactly (validation at line 275, branch at lines 283-285).

The bug is real: the validation `string.IsNullOrEmpty(project) == string.IsNullOrEmpty(group)` treats project="" the same as project=null (both are "empty"), so it only rejects the case where both are empty/null or both are non-empty. It happily accepts project="" (empty string, not null) paired with a valid non-empty group, since IsNullOrEmpty("")=true != IsNullOrEmpty(group)=false.

But the branch selection at line 283 uses `project is not null` rather than `!string.IsNullOrEmpty(project)`. An empty string "" is not null, so this predicate is true, and the code calls `badges.ListForProjectAsync("", name, cancellationToken)` — querying an empty/invalid project — instead of `badges.ListForGroupAsync(group!, ...)`, even though the caller supplied a perfectly valid group and only an empty-string project (which validation itself treated as "absent").

So none of the stated disqualifying conditions apply.

Confirmed as a real, concrete correctness bug at the quoted location.
